Create a processed measurement results object

Source: R/measure-results.R
measure_results.Rd

measure_results() keeps processed measurements together with the column and metadata selections used to interpret them. The measurement data are retained as supplied.

Usage

measure_results(data, measures = NULL, id_cols = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'measure_results'
summary(object, ..., na.rm = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'measure_results'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A baked data frame, a measure_list or measure_nd_list, or a single measure_tbl or measure_nd_tbl.

measures

Name of the measurement column in data. Required when a data frame contains more than one measurement column.

id_cols

Names of sample metadata columns to use when summarizing the results. The default follows measure_summary_table() and keeps scalar columns. Use character() to omit them.

object

A measure_results object.

...

Reserved for method extensions.

na.rm

Whether to omit missing values from the summary statistics.

x

A measure_results object.

Value

An ordinary S3 list with components data, measures, and id_cols, and class measure_results. Subclasses can be added by prefixing the class vector. The original measurement objects, including n-dimensional declarations and value metadata, remain in data.

Details

summary() returns one row per sample using measure_summary_table(). Use ggplot2::autoplot() to draw the selected signal and render_measure_report() to export the summary and plot.

Examples

samples <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = c("A", "B"),
  signal = new_measure_list(list(
    new_measure_tbl(c(210, 254), c(0.12, 0.18)),
    new_measure_tbl(c(210, 254), c(0.20, 0.41))
  ))
)
results <- measure_results(samples, id_cols = "sample_id")
summary(results)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 12
#>   sample_id row_id value_quantity value_unit n_dimensions n_points n_missing
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>          <chr>             <int>    <int>     <int>
#> 1 A              1 NA             NA                    1        2         0
#> 2 B              2 NA             NA                    1        2         0
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_observed <int>, mean <dbl>, sd <dbl>, min <dbl>,
#> #   max <dbl>
results
#> <measure_results>
#>   Members: 2
#>   Dimensions: 1D
#>   Measure column: signal
